findings.title: GitHub user check is skipped on first installation
findings.body: The new authenticated-user check at the end of GitHubInstallation.dispatch only runs when an Integration with the installation_id already exists. When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises DoesNotExist (lines ~481-482), the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately, bypassing the check. The mismatch protection therefore does not apply when the webhook has not yet created the Integration, which is the case the PR says it guards against. The check should run on every path that proceeds to next_step, or the missing-Integration case should be handled explicitly.

findings.title: KeyError when the stored integration has no sender metadata
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is accessed directly. build_integration only sets metadata["sender"] when state contains a sender, so integrations created without one (or with a different metadata shape) will raise KeyError and return a 500 during the install flow instead of the intended error page. Use a safe lookup and fail the pipeline with the error view when the sender is missing.

findings.title: Network failure in the OAuth code exchange is not handled
findings.body: `req = safe_urlopen(...)` is outside the try block, so a connection error or timeout raises an uncaught exception and produces a 500. Only the body read/parse is wrapped. The exchange should be inside the try or otherwise return the error view on failure.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL parameters are not URL-encoded
findings.body: The redirect is built by string formatting: `state` and `redirect_uri` are interpolated into the query string without urlencode. A redirect_uri that contains `&` or `#`, or a state containing reserved characters, would corrupt the authorize request. Build the query with urllib.parse.urlencode.

findings.title: Brittle hard-coded responses.calls index
findings.body: The assertion changed from `responses.calls[0]` to `responses.calls[2]` to check the JWT header. This depends on the exact ordering of mocked HTTP calls, including the new OAuth calls. Any reordering breaks the test without a meaningful reason. Locate the call to the access_tokens endpoint by URL instead.

findings.title: New OAuth failure paths are not tested
findings.body: The PR lists three failure modes: state mismatch, a failed access_token exchange (wrong or reused code), and a GitHub user mismatch. Only the user mismatch is tested, and only on the reinstall path. There is no test for a bad state parameter or an access_token exchange that fails. There is also no test for the first-installation case where no Integration exists yet, which is the bypass described above.
